Only how bright the display is
Only which processor brand is installed
Only how fast a fan rotates
questions.explanation: Privacy addresses appropriate handling of information relating to people.

questions.question: Are security and privacy identical?
options: No, secure storage alone does not justify every collection or use
Yes, every encrypted database is automatically appropriate
Yes, privacy only means antivirus installation
No, because privacy never concerns information
questions.explanation: Security safeguards and appropriate personal-data use are related but distinct.

questions.question: What is data minimisation?
options: Collecting all available personal details by default
Limiting data to what is appropriate for a stated purpose
Publishing every account field
Keeping unnecessary copies indefinitely
questions.explanation: Collecting fewer unnecessary details reduces avoidable exposure.

questions.question: Which dataset suits a public classroom demonstration?
options: Fictional records with only needed fields
Real students' identity numbers
Unredacted family contact lists
A private staff payroll
questions.explanation: Fictional minimal data can teach the task without disclosing real records.

questions.question: What should be checked before sharing a document link?
options: Only the document icon
Audience and view or edit permissions
Only the browser's theme
Only the monitor size
questions.explanation: Link access can extend beyond the intended audience if roles are wrong.

questions.question: Can comments in a document disclose information?
options: No, only the first visible heading can disclose data
No, comments are always automatically public-safe
Yes, review comments and other included material
Yes, but only when printed in red
questions.explanation: Content outside the main body can still contain private details.

questions.question: Does removing a name always make a record unidentifiable?
options: Yes, every remaining field is automatically anonymous
Yes, photographs cannot identify anyone
No, other details may reveal the person
No, because names can never be removed
questions.explanation: Identification can arise from combinations of remaining information.

questions.question: Are all cookies malware?
options: Yes, every cookie is an executable virus
Yes, a website cannot use cookies for sessions
No, because browsers cannot store data
No, cookies have different uses and properties
questions.explanation: Cookies should be assessed by their actual purpose and handling.

questions.question: Does private browsing provide universal anonymity?
options: Yes, websites cannot receive any requests
No, it does not hide activity from every external party
Yes, network operators cannot observe any activity
No, because it permanently publishes all history
questions.explanation: Private mode has a limited browser-session scope.

questions.question: What should a privacy setting be understood through?
options: Only its colour
Only the length of its label
Its supported scope and limitations
A guarantee that all tracking everywhere stops
questions.explanation: Settings cannot be assumed to control every service or observer.

questions.question: Does permission for one use automatically permit every future use?
options: No, review the proposed purpose and permission
Yes, permission is unlimited forever
Yes, a photograph has no audience restrictions
No, because permission can never be given
questions.explanation: Permission should match the intended use and relevant requirements.

questions.question: What should follow an accidental private-data disclosure?
options: Copy it into more public groups
Ignore every institutional procedure
Ask classmates to repost it
Report it through the approved responsible channel
questions.explanation: Timely authorised handling can limit further exposure.

questions.question: What does computer ethics address?
options: Only the speed of a graphics card
Responsible decisions and effects of computing
Only installing decorative fonts
Only counting physical cables
questions.explanation: Ethics considers responsibilities and effects on people.

questions.question: Does technical possibility alone justify an action?
options: Yes, any reachable account may be used
Yes, software capability overrides all rules
No, permission and consequences still matter
No, because computers cannot perform actions
questions.explanation: Capability is not a complete ethical justification.

questions.question: Which is honest academic conduct?
options: Claim every copied solution as original
Invent test results
Identify permitted source material and describe one's own contribution accurately
Remove all source credits to look original
questions.explanation: Honesty requires accurate representation of work and evidence.

questions.question: Does attribution automatically permit every use of an image?
options: Yes, a creator's name removes every restriction
Yes, all online photographs are public domain
No, permission or licence conditions also need checking
No, because creators can never permit reuse
questions.explanation: Credit and permission are different requirements.

questions.question: What does publicly accessible code imply?
options: It is automatically unrestricted for every purpose
It can be viewed, while reuse rights still need review
It always has no author
It can never have a licence
questions.explanation: Access alone does not settle reuse conditions.

questions.question: What should a student do after finding an exposed private folder?
options: Copy all records to a public group
Report it responsibly without exploring unrelated contents
Assume exposure grants permission
Try other users' passwords
questions.explanation: Responsible reporting respects access boundaries.

questions.question: Which design improves an error message's accessibility?
options: Colour alone with no explanation
An unexplained disappearing icon
A meaningful text explanation as well as colour
A warning visible only after guessing a shortcut
questions.explanation: Multiple clear cues help users interpret the problem.

questions.question: Does automation remove responsibility for unfair outcomes?
options: No, data and design still need review
Yes, all automated decisions are inherently fair
Yes, a computer cannot repeat a bias
No, because software cannot support decisions
questions.explanation: Human choices affect data, rules and use of the result.

questions.question: Which test record is ethical?
options: A fabricated success screenshot
A hidden deletion of every failed case
The actual observed failure and its conditions
A claim of universal success after no test
questions.explanation: Accurate records support review and correction.

questions.question: What should follow discovery of an error in a published result?
options: Keep the false claim to protect appearances
Blame an unrelated user without evidence
Invent supporting measurements
Correct the record and explain the relevant limitation
questions.explanation: Accountability includes correcting known errors.

questions.question: Which communication respects others?
options: Publishing threats to win an argument
A clear disagreement without harassment or impersonation
Pretending to be another student
Exposing private details as a joke
questions.explanation: Respectful participation avoids misleading and harmful conduct.

questions.question: What should a project record include?
options: Only promotional claims
Only the developer's favourite colour
Permitted sources, real test outcomes and limitations
Only invented user feedback
questions.explanation: A useful record allows others to assess both work and constraints.

questions.question: Which is a cybercrime example for introductory study?
options: Opening one's own permitted practice file
Writing an original classroom report
Unauthorised access to another person's system
Changing one's own permitted wallpaper
questions.explanation: Unauthorised digital acts can fall within cybercrime law depending on facts and provisions.

questions.question: Does every suspected incident prove a named person's guilt?
options: No, legal findings require appropriate evidence and process
Yes, an online rumour settles the case
Yes, one unverified screenshot proves every allegation
No, because digital evidence can never matter
questions.explanation: Observations and allegations must be distinguished from legal conclusions.

questions.question: Where should current Pakistani reporting information be checked?
options: Only an old forwarded image
Only an anonymous comment
Current official Pakistani sources
Only a fictional exercise sheet
questions.explanation: Official information is the appropriate starting point for current procedures.

questions.question: Does permission to read a sample folder necessarily allow deletion?
options: Yes, all access always means full control
Yes, reading automatically grants administrator rights
No, because folders cannot be read
No, permitted actions have a defined scope
questions.explanation: Authorisation should specify the allowed resources and actions.

questions.question: Which setting suits a classroom security exercise?
options: An unrelated public server without permission
An approved environment with explicit scope
A classmate's private account
A random shop's payment system
questions.explanation: Prepared authorised environments support learning within agreed boundaries.

questions.question: What is identity misuse in a digital context?
options: Accurately identifying oneself in a permitted task
Using another person's identity improperly for a deceptive purpose
Writing fictional names in a worksheet
Changing a sample document title
questions.explanation: Identity misuse concerns an improper use of someone else's identifying information.

questions.question: How should an unexpected payment request be verified?
options: Through only the suspicious message's new number
By replying with a password
By sending money before checking
Through an independently known legitimate contact
questions.explanation: An independent channel reduces reliance on the potentially deceptive request.

questions.question: Which detail may help document an incident?
options: Invented claims about a suspect
Unrelated classmates' passwords
A fabricated receipt
Relevant timestamps and message or transaction references
questions.explanation: Relevant factual records can support authorised investigation.

questions.question: Should original incident evidence be edited to look more convincing?
options: Yes, change figures to strengthen the story
No, preserve it accurately and record context
Yes, remove every uncertainty
No, because context is never useful
questions.explanation: Alteration can damage the reliability of evidence.

questions.question: What is responsible institutional reporting?
options: Publish private records to a public forum
Threaten a suspected person
Run unapproved attacks in response
Notify the authorised contact through the approved procedure
questions.explanation: The responsible process supports investigation while limiting additional harm.

questions.question: Why avoid fixed penalty claims from old social posts?
options: Every online penalty chart is automatically official
Law and procedures may have changed or been misrepresented
Legal rules never change
All offences have one identical penalty
questions.explanation: Current primary sources are needed for actual legal information.

questions.question: What should a factual report distinguish?
options: Only assumptions presented as certainty
Only rumours copied repeatedly
Only personal insults
Observed facts, uncertainty and actions already taken
questions.explanation: Clear distinctions help a reviewer assess what is actually known.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: What should a workstation review consider?
options: The person, equipment, environment and task together
Only the brand logo
Only the wallpaper
Only the number of stickers
questions.explanation: Comfort and risk depend on the overall arrangement and use.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: Which adjustment can reduce unnecessary leaning to read?
options: Making every letter smaller
Moving the mouse farther away
Hiding all document headings
An appropriate text size and readable display arrangement
questions.explanation: Readable content can reduce the need for an awkward viewing position.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: What can glare interfere with?
options: Only the number of stored files
Comfortable viewing of the display
Only a password's length
Only a CPU instruction format
questions.explanation: Lighting and reflections can affect display comfort and readability.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: Where should a pointing device be arranged?
options: Within comfortable reach for the task
As far away as the cable allows
On an unstable edge by default
Behind the monitor in every case
questions.explanation: Avoiding sustained awkward reach is a useful workstation principle.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: Is one fixed posture a universal solution for every user?
options: Yes, everyone has identical body dimensions
No, fit and variation matter
Yes, movement is always harmful
No, because workstation arrangement never matters
questions.explanation: Users and tasks differ, and prolonged static positioning can be uncomfortable.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: What is a useful work-routine principle?
options: Avoid every change of position
Continue through all persistent pain
Vary tasks and include appropriate breaks or changes of activity
Replace every break with the same awkward phone posture
questions.explanation: Variation can reduce prolonged exposure to the same demands.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: Does switching to a phone always provide a useful change from screen work?
options: No, it can repeat similar visual and postural demands
Yes, all phone use automatically rests every muscle
Yes, a smaller screen eliminates strain
No, because phones have no screens
questions.explanation: The actual activity and posture determine whether demands have changed.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: Why can extended laptop work require adaptation?
options: The attached screen and keyboard constrain their independent positions
Laptops never contain keyboards
Every laptop must be held in the air
Laptops cannot display text
questions.explanation: Combined components can make arranging both viewing and input more difficult.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: What is appropriate for cables across a walkway?
options: Leave them because software is working
Pull live electrical equipment apart
Report or arrange them safely through approved procedures
Cover them with loose papers
questions.explanation: Physical workstation safety includes avoiding trip hazards.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: Should a student open powered equipment to improve comfort?
options: Yes, every discomfort requires opening the PSU
Yes, any cable can be repaired while powered
No, use authorised maintenance and adjustment procedures
No, because chairs cannot be adjusted
questions.explanation: Comfort reviews do not justify unsafe electrical or hardware work.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: What should persistent pain or visual problems prompt?
options: A guaranteed diagnosis from a worksheet
Appropriate reporting and qualified health advice
Ignoring every symptom indefinitely
An unverified online cure as certainty
questions.explanation: Persistent symptoms need appropriate individual assessment.

questions.topic: 7.9 Health Concerns and Comfortable Computer Use
questions.question: How should the cited UK workstation guidance be used here?
options: As proof of identical legal rights in every country
As practical learning guidance without claiming its laws apply in Pakistan
As a diagnosis of every student's condition
As a substitute for all individual assessment
questions.explanation: Practical principles and jurisdiction-specific legal duties must be distinguished.
